newsitem.title: USA: GTSI Inc sees Q4 loss of $15 mln.
newsitem.headline: GTSI Inc sees Q4 loss of $15 mln.

text.p: Government Technology Services Inc said Friday that due to a decline in sales and certain fourth quarter charges, it expects a net loss of $15 million in the fourth quarter of 1996, ended December 31, and a net loss of approximately $17.6 million for the year.
This compares with a 1995 fourth quarter net loss of $4.2 million and a net loss of $7.2 million for the year.

The company also said it expects revenues of about $145 million for the 1996 fourth quarter and about $492 million for the year, compared with revenues revenues of $160 million for the fourth quarter of 1995 and $527 million for the year.
The company plans to release final, audited results in approximately three weeks.

Fourth quarter and annual sales were negatively impacted by reduced shipments, as new ID/IQ contracts did not produce sufficient revenues in 1996 to replace the GTSI's 1995 Air Force Desktop IV contract revenues, said the company.

The company said results reflect a fourth quarter pretax charge, estimated at $14.3 million, related to revaluation of intangible assets, the previously announced settlement of the Air Force DTIV contract dispute, severance and other charges related to operations.

The charges included in fourth quarter results will cause the company to be out of compliance with a covenant in its loan agreement. GTSI said its lead bank has indicated that it intends to issue a waiver in this regard.
GTSI also said that for reasons unrelated to the above financial results, its chief financial officer, Peter Janke, is leaving on April 19, as previously announced.
